description.txt: The reference architecture: warehouse-style governance and query over open table formats on object storage. Assembled from OSS foundations plus the connective tissue they don't ship.

Decides 'can this principal do this here?' and, when allowed, governs what they see (row filters, column masks). A cross-cutting zero-trust decomposition (PAP / PDP / PEP / PIP) whose points are realized by different services per deployment.
Authors and distributes policy. Today: the Cedar policy set + schema published as an OCI bundle. The versioned, fast-push control plane with a freshness SLA is designed, not built.

Decides allow/deny and computes fine-grained constraints (row filters, column masks) from the policy + facts. NIST 800-207 'Policy Engine'. Today embedded (in-process Cedar); a central/hybrid topology is designed.

Enforces the PDP's decision — rewrites the query plan to inject filters/masks and short-circuits on deny. Realized as the engine PEP (in-plan) and, at the network edge, the gateway PEP (ext_authz). An agent-tool PEP is designed.

Supplies the facts a decision needs. The catalog is the authoritative resource.* PIP (table identity, ownership, classification tags); identity PIP is built (v1); network (in_trusted_environment) and session/lineage PIPs are designed.

Acts on the PDP's verdict. NIST 800-207 'Policy Administrator': the catalog's credential-vending path mints a short-lived scoped credential only after an authorize check. A guard making governed tables non-vendable to coarse-only consumers is designed.
Queries and governs data over open table formats — the human consumer of the lakehouse.
Builds and operates the lakehouse services; the primary audience for this model.
Consumes the lakehouse through agent-optimized CLIs and MCP surfaces. The 'and AI' half of open-lakehouse-and-ai.
The shared query/compute core the query engine is built on. Policy and lineage plug in via its extension points.
An open table format (via delta-rs / delta-kernel-rs). Realizes the tableFormat capability.
An open table format. Realizes the tableFormat capability; reached in the estate via Iceberg-REST catalogs (e.g. Lakekeeper).
The policy language and decision engine behind the governance PDP.
The lineage event standard the lineage capability emits and ingests. Marquez is the reference server it's inspired by.
The governance API surface the catalog builds and integrates with — and explores ahead of — rather than competing with the official Java implementation.
An Iceberg-REST catalog. The catalog's Delta API can feed it (feasibility-stage interop) so Iceberg-REST consumers see the same tables.
An external query engine that can receive a vended scoped storage credential and read raw files. Enforces only coarse access — FGAC (row filters / column masks) is bypassed when it reads directly.
Governs tables, schemas, and credentials. The surface every query resolves through; issues short-lived scoped storage credentials at resolution time (credential vending).
Resolves tables through the catalog and executes over open table formats. Catalog-native: credentials, policy, and lineage attach at resolution/planning time.

Gives raw object-storage bytes table semantics — ACID transactions, schema, and snapshots. The technology-agnostic 'open table format' layer; Delta and Iceberg are peer concrete formats that realize it.
The byte container where table data files are written. Beneath the table format — the format is what makes these bytes a governed, transactional table.
Captures dataset- and column-level provenance (OpenLineage) at query planning time — 'where did this data come from, and where does it flow'.
